newsitem.title: USA: MOTOR RACING-TRACY USES 'HOME' ADVANTAGE IN FASTEST PRACTICE.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-TRACY USES 'HOME' ADVANTAGE IN FASTEST PRACTICE.

text.p: Canadian Paul Tracy used some "home" advantage on Friday to post the fastest time in practice for Sunday's CART Indy car race.

Tracy, who as a test driver for team owner Roger Penske, whose company owns this track, has driven thousands of miles here, lapped the one-mile oval in 19.024 seconds (189.235 mph/304.5 kph),in a Penske Mercedes-Benz.
Canadian rookie Patrick Carpentier was second fastest in a Reynard Mercedes-Benz at 19.301.
Penske stalwart Al Unser Jr., a two-time Indy 500 winner, was third fastest at 19.483, followed by a real native of Nazareth, Michael Andretti, in a Swift Ford at 19.663.
Tracy said he could not say how many laps he'd run in pre-season testing for the Penske team but he estimated that in 1994 alone he drove 3,000 to 4,000 miles here.
"We've done our homework. Paul has done a lot of testing here," said Unser. "We've opened up the weekend strong and if we can keep it like that over the next two days, we should be where we belong."
The once powerful Penske team has been in somewhat of a drought of late with no wins in 1996, the first time in 20 years the team failed to win one race.
"Confidence is the key," said Tracy. "We've just got to get that monkey off our back."
Single car qualifying for Sunday's 225-mile (362 km) race will take place on Saturday afternoon.
